THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 10.01.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA.76/2014  3  2025:KER:1742  JUDGMENT Dated this the 10th day of January, 2025
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.149/2010 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ottappalam is the appellant herein.

The respondents in the O.P.
are the respondents herein.

The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in the accident that occurred on 5.1.2010.
2.

According to the petitioner, on 5.1.2010 at 2 p.m., while he was riding a motorcycle bearing No.
KL-8-AG-3729 along the public road and when he reached the accident spot, another motor cycle bearing registration No.KL-8-1340 ridden by the 1 st respondent in a rash and negligent manner came from the opposite direction and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.
As a result of which, he fell down and sustained serious injuries.
The 2nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the him, 2025:KER:1742 the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, he filed the OP claiming a compensation of Rs.2,75,000/-.
3. The 1st and 2nd respondents remained ex-parte.
The 3rd respondent/insurer alone contested the matter before the Tribunal.
3 rd respondent admitted the accident and policy and contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.

sentences.text:
The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PWs 1 and 2 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A12 and B1.
5.
After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,96,700/-.
6. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

7. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

8. Heard Sri. Sheji P. Abraham, the learned Counsel appearing for 2025:KER:1742 the appellant,
and Sri. N.S. Mohammed Usman, learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
9.
The Point: In this case the accident and valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
Though in the written statement the 3 rd respondent has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner, at the time of arguments such a contention was not taken.
The petitioner has produced Ext.A5, copy of the final report in the crime registered against the driver of the offending vehicle, in respect to the above accident.

In the light of the above final report,
negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle stands proved.
Therefore, the 3rd respondent, being the insurer, is liable to indemnify the compensation, which is liable to be awarded against the owner of the offending vehicle.
10. One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that the notional income fixed by the Tribunal is on the lesser side.
The petitioner was aged 23 years on the date of the accident, on 5.10.2010.
According to the petitioner, he was working as an 2025:KER:1742 Electrician, earning Rs.8,000/- per month.
However, the Tribunal fixed his income at Rs.4,000/-.

As per the dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v.
Manger, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a Coolie in the year 2010 is 7500/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the petitioner could not prove the claim that he is an Electrician, his notional income is liable to be fixed at Rs.7500/- as that of a Coolie during the year 2010.

11. As per Exhibit A8 series discharge summaries, the petitioner sustained type III open fracture both bones (left) leg with avulsion crack fracture fibular head (L) with foot drop, internal degloving injury (L) leg with early compartment syndrome.

A9 disability certificate was issued by the Associate Professor of Orthopaedics attached to Medical College Hospital, Thrissur, who was examined as PW2 and he, deposed before the Court that the petitioner could not stand for a long time and he cannot climb steps.
The petitioner cannot move the toes of his left leg due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
It was in the above context, 2025:KER:1742 the permanent disability of the petitioner was assessed at 10%.

The Tribunal accepted the same and I do not find any grounds to Linson vs Ratheeshkumar on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46058594/
3 interfere with the same.

sentences.text:
12. Since, on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 23 years, 40% of his income is to be added towards future prospects, and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].
13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, compensation towards loss of disability will come to Rs.2,26,800/-.
14. Towards loss of earnings, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/- at the rate of Rs.4000/- for a period of five months.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the period of loss of earnings is to be enhanced as the injuries suffered by the petitioner was severe.
Considering the facts, I hold that the income for the period of six months @Rs.7500 can be awarded on the head loss of earnings, which will come to Rs.45,000/- (7500x6).
15. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has 2025:KER:1742 awarded only Rs.20,000/-.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, I hold that compensation towards pain and suffering awarded is on the lower side and hence it is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
16.
Towards the head compensation for loss of amenities, the Tribunal has not awarded any amount.
The petitioner was treated as an inpatient for 17 days.
Because of the injuries sustained by him, he had to take rest for a considerable period.
PW2 deposed before the Court that the petitioner could not stand for a long time and he cannot climb steps.
The petitioner cannot move the toes of his left leg due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
He suffered permanent disability assessed at 10%.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, I hold that towards compensation for loss of amenities Rs.30,000/- can be awarded.
17. Towards extra nourishment, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.4,000/-.
The petitioner was hospitalised as inpatient for 17 days and he had to take rest for about 6 months.

Considering the nature of 2025:KER:1742 injuries sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, the compensation awarded for extra nourishment is on the lesser side, and hence it is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-.
18. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
19. Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.4,38,100/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.
Sl. Head of claim Amount awarded by The amount give

No. the Tribunal (Rs) in appeal (Rs.
 1 Loss of earnings 20,000/- 45,000/-

2 Medical & miscellaneous Expenses 56,800/- 56,800/-
 3

Personal assistance 4,000/- 4,000/-
 4

Transportation expenses 5,000/- 5,000/-

4

5 Extra nourishment 4,000/- 20,000/-
 6 Damage to clothing etc. 500/- 500/-
 7 Pain and suffering 20,000/- 50,000/-
 8

Compensation for permanent disability 86,400/- 2,26,800/-
 9 Loss of amenities NIL 30,000/-

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3 rd 2025:KER:1742 respondent is directed to deposit a total compensation of Rs.4,38,100/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Thirty Eight Thousand One Hundred Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till realisation, excluding interest for a period of 83 days,
the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
(Interest for the enhanced compensation is limited to 8%)

On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable,
if any, without delay, as per rules.
